gist: Antarctic winter sea ice reached its third-lowest peak on record on 14 September.
The last four years have recorded the four lowest winter sea ice levels.
Scientists warn that climate warming is driving persistent changes in Antarctic ice.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Antarctic winter sea ice peaked at 17.59m square kilometres on 14 September, reaching its third-lowest maximum level since satellite monitoring began in 1979. The peak was about one million square kilometres below the long-term average. The four lowest maximum levels on record have all occurred over the past four years.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Less sea ice allows the ocean to absorb more solar heat and exposes ice shelves to buffeting ocean extremes. Weakened ice shelves could accelerate glacier melting and raise global sea levels. Unstable sea ice also threatens critical habitats for species including krill, algae and emperor penguins.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Since peaking, the sea ice has been dropping faster than usual, leading scientists to warn of another low summer. Researchers are still working to quantify how sensitive the global climate system is to this loss of sea ice.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Douglas Stewart Carter was released from a Utah county jail after spending more than four decades on death row. He was originally convicted in 1985 for killing Eva Olesen, based on a confession and witness testimony that was later recanted. Although tried again in 1992 and found guilty, the state supreme court ordered a new trial due to investigator misconduct. Recent DNA analysis excluded Carter as a match to blood on a doorknob and genetic material on a knife handle.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The new DNA evidence undermined the original case against Carter, leading prosecutors to withdraw their intent to seek the death penalty and agree that reassessing his bail was necessary. However, the victim's family expressed serious concerns and a desire for concrete answers and justice.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Carter must wear a GPS monitoring device until a new trial begins. A retrial was scheduled for 2027, while his attorney urges prosecutors to seek dismissal of the pending aggravated murder charge.

sections.text: US cafe and shop owners are facing a wave of lawsuits alleging violations of Title III of the Americans With Disabilities Act (ADA). sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Fighting these lawsuits in court or paying out private settlements involves thousands of dollars in legal fees, which can threaten the survival of small businesses. sections.text: Patricio Guzmán, who died aged 85, directed documentary films chronicling Salvador Allende's government and General Augusto Pinochet's bloody coup. sections.heading: Why it matters
